title: Saudi Arabia hosts Jeddah talks on Ukraine with national security advisers
body:
Saudi Arabia hosted a two-day meeting in Jeddah on 5 and 6 August 2023 of national security advisers and diplomatic representatives from about 40 countries and international organisations to discuss a negotiated settlement of the war in Ukraine. It was the second such meeting, after an earlier gathering in Copenhagen in June, which had fewer participants. The talks were described as part of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's efforts to facilitate peace since March 2022.

Ukraine took part. Russia was excluded. Representatives of the United States, China and India attended. Andriy Yermak, head of the office of Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, said the talks involved "very productive consultations on the key principles on which a just and lasting peace should be built". Zelensky's peace formula was examined, and Ukraine hoped the talks would lead to a peace summit later in 2023.

Saudi Arabia said participants agreed on the importance of continuing international consultation to build common ground toward peace. China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Wang Wenbin said China was willing to play a constructive role in a political solution. Moscow called the talks a "doomed Western attempt to align the Global South" behind Kyiv. Saudi analyst Salman Al Ansari said he did not expect an immediate breakthrough.
